parameters.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal runaway to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, including incidents involving injury, property damage, or suspected product malfunction. Within 72 hours, the manufacturer must notify affected customers and provide immediate safety instructions when continued use may pose a risk.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal runaway to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, including incidents involving injury, property damage, or suspected product malfunction. Within 72 hours, the manufacturer must notify affected customers and provide immediate safety instructions when continued use may pose a risk.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal runaway to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, including incidents involving injury, property damage, or suspected product malfunction. The manufacturer must provide an initial incident report even when the cause is not yet established, and update it as material facts emerge. Within 72 hours, the manufacturer must notify affected customers and provide immediate safety instructions when continued use may pose a risk. Reports must identify the affected model and batch to regulators; public notices must not disclose individual customers’ personal information.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Each model must undergo sustained-heat testing at 55 °C before sale and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-recognized representative protocol and sample. A model exceeding a 5% failure rate must be retested and the manufacturer must submit a corrective-action plan to the regulator; customers of that model must be promptly notified of the results and relevant safety precautions.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo sustained-heat testing at 55 °C before sale and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-recognized representative protocol and sample. Manufacturers must submit per-model results, including sample size, failure count, test date, and protocol, to the relevant regulator and provide those results to customers of that model. A model exceeding a 5% failure rate must be retested and the manufacturer must submit a corrective-action plan to the regulator; customers of that model must be promptly notified of the results and relevant safety precautions. Material model changes require retesting before sale.

parameters.quote: New units must support a secure remote emergency shut-off that can place the battery in a safe state without creating additional hazards. Existing installed units must be upgraded to support remote shut-off, or an equivalent safe emergency-isolation capability, within six years after adoption of this standard.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: New units must support a secure remote emergency shut-off that can place the battery in a safe state without creating additional hazards. Existing installed units must be upgraded to support remote shut-off, or an equivalent safe emergency-isolation capability, within six years after adoption of this standard.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New units must support a secure remote emergency shut-off that can place the battery in a safe state without creating additional hazards. Manufacturers must provide clear instructions for using it and maintain an emergency response process. Existing installed units must be upgraded to support remote shut-off, or an equivalent safe emergency-isolation capability, within six years after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers must notify owners of the capability, limitations, and any required upgrade.

parameters.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers must document that suppression systems are tested for compatibility with the battery and do not create additional hazards. Units manufactured before the effective date are not subject to this requirement.

parameters.quote: If a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the regulator must promptly review the evidence and require appropriate corrective action; a recall is required when the regulator determines the risk warrants removal from service, considering incident severity, validated rates, and available mitigations. Customers must receive clear safety notices promptly when a material model-specific safety risk is identified, including relevant test findings, affected units, and recommended precautions.

Customers must receive clear safety notices promptly when a material model-specific safety risk is identified, including relevant test findings, affected units, and recommended precautions.

S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Customers must receive clear safety notices promptly when a material model-specific safety risk is identified, including relevant test findings, affected units, and recommended precautions. Manufacturers must notify regulators and affected customers of corrective actions and recall decisions. If a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the regulator must promptly review the evidence and require appropriate corrective action; a recall is required when the regulator determines the risk warrants removal from service, considering incident severity, validated rates, and available mitigations. Manufacturers must promptly notify customers if a recall is ordered and provide instructions and remedies.

judge_section_notes: S1 is strict: all incidents reported to the regulator within 24 hours, customers notified within 72 hours, and reporting required while the cause is under investigation. S2 sets 55 °C testing and a 5% failure-rate threshold, but exceeding it triggers only retesting and a corrective-action plan, not a sales stop, while per-model numeric results go to customers but not the public. S3 requires new-unit shut-off from adoption and a 6-year retrofit deadline. S4 requires built-in fire suppression at 36 months. S5 has an 8/100k review trigger, but recall is discretionary and corrective action can replace recall indefinitely; customer notices are only 'promptly'.
